New keyframe: after the 25 April 1974 revolution and the Guinea-Bissau recognition of 26 August 1974 (Colonial War page).

region.text: metropolitan Portugal and the overseas possessions, as Cliopatria's first Estado Novo shape draws them

ledger.note: 1926: the 28 May 1926 coup ends the First Republic and starts the Ditadura Militar; the state, its capital and its overseas possessions carry over unchanged. Page names Angola, Mozambique, Portuguese Guinea, Timor, Portuguese India and Dadra and Nagar Haveli as the overseas possessions.
1928: the Ditadura Militar 'became the Ditadura Nacional in 1928'; colour and dossier continue.
1933: the corporatist constitution is approved by referendum on 19 March 1933 and the Estado Novo is established (infobox 'Established: 11 April 1933'); same state, new regime.

1942: Japan invades Portuguese Timor; the page says a British, Australian and Dutch force had occupied it in December 1941 'to preempt a Japanese invasion' and that 'the Japanese did invade in the Battle of Timor in February 1942'. Portuguese sovereignty continued; infobox 'Japanese occupation of Portuguese Timor: 1942-45'.
1945: the Japanese occupation ends; 'Following World War II, the Portuguese promptly returned to reclaim their colony' (the page gives no year or month; infobox '1942-45').

region.text: Dadra and Nagar Haveli, the enclaves of Portuguese India inland of Daman

ledger.note: 1954: Dadra and Nagar Haveli pass to India. 'Pro-Indian forces occupied them in 1954'; Nagar Haveli's Portuguese administrator and police surrendered on 11 August 1954.

region.text: the Fort of Sao Joao Baptista de Ajuda

ledger.note: 1961: 'In August 1961, the Dahomey annexed the Fort of Sao Joao Baptista de Ajuda' at Ouidah, a few hectares not drawn on Cliopatria's shapes.
1961: Operation Vijay begins; 'hostilities began at 09:45 on 17 December' 1961.
1961: the Portuguese governor general Manuel Antonio Vassalo e Silva signs the instrument of surrender on 19 December 1961 at 20:30.

region.text: Goa, Daman and Diu, the 'State of India'

ledger.note: 1961: India annexes Goa, Daman and Diu (about 4,000 km2); the page: 'in December that year India annexed Goa, Daman, and Diu'. Portugal recognised Indian sovereignty by a treaty signed 31 December 1974. Cliopatria keeps the three districts in the Estado Novo shape until 1966.

1974: the Carnation Revolution of 25 April 1974, a coup by the Armed Forces Movement, 'led to the end of the Estado Novo'; the Third Portuguese Republic begins the same day. Same state, new regime: colour continues.

1974: Guinea-Bissau. Part of the territory was independent de facto in 1973 (Carnation Revolution page); under the Algiers accord Portugal agreed to recognise the Guinea-Bissau government 'on 26 August 1974' (Colonial War page). Cliopatria keeps it in the shape to 1975.
1975: Angola becomes a People's Republic ('Angola and Mozambique became People's Republics in 1975'); the pages opened give no day.
1975: Mozambique becomes a People's Republic; the pages opened give no day.

1975: Cape Verde 'independence in 1975' (Carnation Revolution page; no day). [Reviewer eu-21-c, 2026-10-31: counterpart 'cape-verde' changed to the existing dossier republic-of-cabo-verde, whose found event names estado-novo]
1975: Sao Tome and Principe 'independence in 1975' (Carnation Revolution page; no day).
1975: Fretilin 'unilaterally declared the colony's independence' on 28 November 1975 after a UDT coup in August; on 7 December 1975 'the Indonesian Armed Forces launched an invasion of East Timor'.
1976: Indonesia 'formally annexed East Timor, declaring it as its 27th province' on 17 July 1976; the UN did not recognise it and kept Portugal as the Administering Power.
1976: Portuguese Timor passes to Indonesian control; de jure Portugal remained the Administering Power in the UN's view.

1999: Macau 'officially occurred at midnight on 20 December 1999': the handover to China. Portugal had withdrawn its troops on 31 December 1975 and from 1976 both governments called Macau a 'Chinese territory under Portuguese supervision'; de jure Portuguese rule lasted until the handover.

wars.name: Annexation of Goa
wars.outcome: India took Portuguese India on 17-19 December 1961 (Operation Vijay); Portugal recognised the annexation by treaty on 31 December 1974.
wars.note: Dadra and Nagar Haveli had fallen to pro-Indian forces on 11 August 1954.

wars.name: Portuguese Colonial War
wars.outcome: Military stalemate and a rebel political victory; the 25 April 1974 coup ended it and the African territories became independent 1974-1975.
wars.note: Infobox start 4 February 1961 (Angola); PAIGC fighting from January 1963; first FRELIMO attack 25 September 1964.

wars.name: Japanese occupation of Portuguese Timor
wars.outcome: Japan occupied Portuguese Timor from February 1942 to 1945; the Portuguese returned after the war.
wars.note: Portugal was neutral; a British, Australian and Dutch force had landed in December 1941. [Reviewer eu-21-c, 2026-10-31: belligerent kingdom-of-great-britain (ends 1800) changed to united-kingdom.]

wars.name: Indonesian invasion of East Timor
wars.outcome: Indonesia invaded on 7 December 1975 and annexed East Timor on 17 July 1976; the UN did not recognise it and kept Portugal as Administering Power.

certainty.note: Colonial frontiers are modern treaty lines in the era; none of the pages opened gives a boundary, so this rests on the era. Timor in 1975-1976 and Macau 1976-1999 (a 'Chinese territory under Portuguese supervision') are administrative, not sovereign, borders.

notes: One dossier for the Portuguese state from the 28 May 1926 coup to 2024: Cliopatria's Estado Novo row names a regime that ended on 25 April 1974 but is the only row that carries Portugal after 1925, so the Third Republic is a rename event (rule 2) and the 1979-2024 Cabinda patch is judged wrong. Dossier name and Cliopatria Name differ on purpose. Page budget (9) spent on 8 pages: Estado Novo, Portuguese Empire, Colonial War, Carnation Revolution, Annexation of Goa, Portuguese Timor, Handover of Macau, Third Portuguese Republic. Page silent: exact independence days for Cape Verde, Sao Tome, Mozambique and Angola (1975 only; month omitted), Macau in the Second World War, the 1951 overseas-provinces reform, Azores and Madeira autonomy. Counterparts needing dossiers: cape-verde, republic-of-dahomey (Ajuda 1961). Cliopatria 'Macao' 1 cell and 'Timor' 52 cells sit inside the Estado Novo shape. The end year 2024 is Cliopatria's last year.
